title: POC customer activation timeline and daybook
content:
Overview:
This document is the working activation timeline and daybook for the AcmeCorp POC (customer-facing pilot) running Redwood inference in a Dedicated capacity with a Private control-plane evaluation. Purpose is to track daily tasks, decisions, risks, and stakeholder checkpoints across a condensed 6-week engagement with emphasis on performance SLOs and secure networking.

Goals and success criteria (explicit):
- Demonstrate 99% of inference requests under 220ms p95 for 2k concurrent users on Acme test harness.
- Verify end-to-end data isolation: VPC peering + KMS integration with customer-owned key.
- Conduct one canary rollout and one failover test to hosted fallback within engagement window.
- Pass QA acceptance: 10 av-critical prompts with no regression vs baseline model (quality threshold > 0.92).

Scope (what's in / out):
In scope:
- Dedicated GPU pool sizing and smoke benchmarking (g4dn-ish baseline).
- Private control-plane integration with customer network and KMS.
- Production-like traffic replay through Redwood Console, traces enabled.
Out of scope:
- Full production dataset migration (customer will schedule post-POC).
- Long-term chargeback/cost model agreement (to be negotiated if POC passes).

High-level milestone cadence (6-week view):
- Week 0 (Prep): Kickoff, inventory, baseline benchmarks capture (customer test harness), network prechecks.
- Week 1 (Deploy): Private control-plane install + KMS smoke, Dedicated pool allocation, initial model load.
- Week 2 (Tune): Kernel/quant config, batching profiles, first latency/cost sweep.
- Week 3 (Workshops): Two technical workshops (operator runbook + app integration), customer-driven evals.
- Week 4 (Canary & Failover): Canary rollout of tuned model, simulated capacity failover to hosted fallback.
- Week 5 (Acceptance & Handover): Final acceptance runbook, metrics export, next-steps proposal.

Daily daybook template (use this section to record day-by-day):
- Date: YYYY-MM-DD
- Primary focus: (deploy/tune/workshop/test)
- Attendees: names / customer contacts
- Actions completed: bullet list (tickets closed)
- Blocking items: bullet list (owner + ETA)
- Decisions made: short note + rationale
- Metrics snapshot: p50/p95 latency, throughput, error-rate
- Next actions: owner + due date

Example entry (2025-11-18):
- Date: 2025-11-18
- Primary focus: Private control-plane dry-run
- Attendees: Asha Patel, Miguel Santos, Acme infra (N. Kaur), Liam O'Connor
- Actions completed: completed installer run in staging; validated KMS handshake; assigned network CIDR mapping (acme-vpc-1).
- Blocking items: customer firewall needs rule for 10.4.12.0/24 -> assigned to N. Kaur (ETA 11/20).
- Decisions made: use mTLS mutual auth instead of IP-based allowlist to support future ephemeral workers. Rationale: reduces ops friction for customer.
- Metrics snapshot: p95 baseline 360ms (dev harness), initial Dedicated run 280ms p95 with 4x batching disabled.
- Next actions: implement prefix cache (Miguel) due 11/20; create failover policy (Liam) due 11/22.

Task tracker (selected items):
- TASK-001: Private control-plane install in Acme staging – owner: Miguel Santos – status: in_progress – linked: JIRA SE-412
- TASK-002: KMS integration test matrix – owner: Priya Rao – status: in_review – linked: Confluence matrix
- TASK-003: Performance sweep scripts and steady-state runner – owner: Jordan Kim – status: todo – linked: GH PR #58
- TASK-004: Operator workshop slide deck – owner: Asha Patel – status: in_progress – due: 2025-12-03
- TASK-005: Canary rollback policy definition – owner: Liam O'Connor – status: todo – due: 2025-12-10

Workshop agendas (core sessions to run with customer):
- Operator runbook (90m): install review, day-2 ops, autoscale knobs, alerting thresholds, runbook for failover.
- App integration (60m): SDK patterns, prefix caching, request routing policies, streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs.
- Quality & evals (75m): prompt set review, acceptance criteria, regression detection, quality dashboards.

Acceptance checklist (minimal):
- All tests in acceptance harness run (10/10) and pass quality threshold
- Latency SLO verified across three traffic shapes (bursty, steady, ramp)
- KMS-configured keys validated and rotation tested in staging
- Rollout/canary exercised and rollback time measured (<2 minutes to switch to fallback)
- Operational runbook handed to Acme SRE with runbook walkthrough recorded

Risk register (top items):
- Risk: Customer firewall restrictions delay private control-plane connectivity.
  Mitigation: pre-auth tunnel plan (VPN) + fallback plan to temporary hosted endpoint; owner: N. Kaur; severity: high.
- Risk: Quantized model path reduces quality below acceptance.
  Mitigation: keep float/quant pair; if quality delta > 0.03 revert to float; owner: Jordan Kim; severity: medium.
- Risk: Dedicated capacity underprovisioned for replay traffic.
  Mitigation: allocate 25% buffer and allow short burst autoscale policy; owner: Miguel Santos; severity: medium-high.

Decision log (brief):
- 2025-11-15: Selected model variant: open-llama-v2-13b-quant (tuned) + float fallback.
- 2025-11-20: Chose mTLS auth for control-plane connectivity.

Stakeholders and contacts:
- Primary SE (Redwood): Asha Patel – asha@redwood.ai – pager: +1-555-0123
- SE ops lead: Miguel Santos – miguel@redwood.ai
- Customer lead (Acme): Nidhi Kaur – nidhi.kaur@acme.com
- Product sponsor: Liam O'Connor – liam@redwood.ai

Communication plan and cadences:
- Twice-weekly syncs (Mon/Wed 30m) during active deploy/tune phases.
- Dry-run demo at end of Week 2 (internal Redwood + Acme infra).
- Acceptance presentation and executive summary at end of Week 5.

Next steps (immediate priorities):
- Confirm firewall rule ETA with Acme (owner: N. Kaur) – due 2025-11-20
- Miguel to complete installer idempotency fixes in staging – due 2025-11-19
- Jordan to open dataset anonymization checklist (privacy review) – due 2025-11-21

Notes / loose thoughts (scratchpad):
- Consider adding a quick cost-sensitivity table to show per-million-token cost delta for quant vs float in the final slide.
- Capture a short runbook script for rotating keys in KMS during handover (customer security asked for SOP).
- Keep a small recorded demo where we inject latency to show failover path (useful for exec acceptance).

This document is a living daybook — update the daybook section after each major session so rollups can be pasted into the handover briefing.
